I'd be willing to bet it's something to do with the ASD circuit. That shit's a nightmare. They branched a bunch of little wires off one big one that's fused at 30a and driven by a relay. Every intermittent no start problem I've had with Chryslers made between 1977 and 2003 has either been a bad crank/cam sensor, or ASD related. The fix for the ASD nightmare is pulling the engine/trans harness and putting inline fuses at every spot the little wires branch off of the main ASD power wire.
